title: DNS, DHCP, HTTP, email and software-defined networking
subtitle: The protocols you actually see: what happens between typing a name and seeing a page, and how modern networks are managed.

dhcp.title: DHCP: getting an address
dhcp.body: A new host has no IP. DHCP lends one in four messages, known as DORA: Discover (broadcast), Offer, Request, Acknowledge. The lease also carries the subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server, and expires unless renewed.

dns.title: DNS: names to addresses
dns.body: DNS is a distributed hierarchy: root servers know the top-level domains (.com, .np), TLD servers know the domains, and the domain’s authoritative server knows the host. Your machine asks a recursive resolver, which does the walking and caches the answer for its TTL.
dns.steps: A record has TTL 300 s. The resolver answered at t = 0. A query at t = 120 s is answered from the cache; one at t = 400 s triggers a new lookup.

http.title: HTTP and the web
http.body: Typing a URL sets off a chain: DNS finds the IP, TCP connects (TLS for HTTPS), the browser sends GET /page HTTP/1.1 and the server replies with a status line, headers and the body. Methods: GET (read), POST (send), PUT, DELETE. Status families: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error (404), 5xx server error (500). HTTP is stateless; cookies and tokens carry a session.

mail.title: Email: SMTP, POP3, IMAP
mail.body: SMTP pushes mail from your client to your server and between servers. To read it, POP3 downloads messages (usually deleting them from the server) while IMAP keeps them on the server and syncs folders across devices. Other services: FTP moves files; SNMP manages devices; VoIP carries voice over IP.

sdn.title: Software-defined networking
sdn.body: In a traditional router the control plane (route calculation) and data plane (forwarding) live together in each box. SDN separates them: a central controller computes behaviour and programs simple forwarding devices through an API (OpenFlow). Benefits: a global view, automation, rapid change. Related ideas: network virtualisation, content delivery networks (CDNs cache content near users), named-data and intent-based networking.

sec.title: Network security in brief
sec.body: Goals: confidentiality, integrity, authentication, availability. Tools: TLS encrypts a connection; firewalls filter by address, port or application; VPNs tunnel private traffic over the Internet; intrusion detection watches for attacks. The next-generation areas (quantum networks, network virtualisation) build on the same layered ideas.
